annotation:
I was born and raised in a small coastal town in Maine, where the community was tight-knit, and everyone knew each other. My parents were both teachers, and they instilled in me a love for learning from a young age. They always encouraged me to ask questions, explore new ideas, and seek knowledge independently. Growing up, I spent most of my time outdoors, exploring the woods and beaches near our home, developing a deep appreciation for nature.

As I entered high school, I found myself drawn to subjects like literature, history, and science. I excelled academically and became involved in various extracurricular activities, including the debate team, drama club, and environmental club. Through these experiences, I discovered a passion for connecting with others and working collaboratively to tackle complex issues.

When it came time to choose a college, I decided to attend a small liberal arts school in New England. There, I pursued a degree in Environmental Studies and minored in Sociology. During my undergraduate years, I became increasingly committed to sustainability efforts and social justice causes. I participated in several campus organizations focused on climate change awareness, volunteered at local food banks, and even studied abroad in Costa Rica to learn more about sustainable agriculture practices.

Following graduation, I moved to Washington D.C. to work for an environmental advocacy group. In this role, I assisted in organizing campaigns, conducting research, and engaging with policymakers. It was an incredibly rewarding experience, but after a few years, I felt the need to broaden my horizons and explore new opportunities.

I then decided to pursue a Master's degree in Urban Planning, focusing on sustainable urban development. Throughout my studies, I became fascinated by the potential for cities to become more environmentally friendly while also addressing social inequality. My graduate research focused on affordable housing solutions and green infrastructure projects in low-income communities.

After completing my master's program, I accepted a position as a project manager at a design firm specializing in sustainable urban planning. In this role, I have had the opportunity to work on various projects across the country, collaborating with architects, engineers, and community leaders to create innovative, eco-friendly spaces that foster connection and equity.

In my free time, I enjoy hiking, biking, and practicing yoga. I also love reading, attending concerts, and experimenting with vegetarian cooking. Over the years, I have come to value the importance of self-care and maintaining a healthy work-life balance. As I continue to grow both personally and professionally, I remain passionate about making a positive impact on the world through my work and daily choices.
